source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why should a support repair record include what changed and information needed for reversal?

options.text: Recording a change makes every attempted repair automatically reversible.
options.feedback: A record supports reversal where possible but does not guarantee it. The workflow must preserve information relevant to the actual change.

options.text: A change record replaces the need to inspect the repaired object.
options.feedback: Logging and verification serve different purposes. The record documents the action; inspecting the object checks whether it worked.

options.text: The record lets the agent apply unfamiliar repairs without escalation.
options.feedback: Documentation does not turn an unknown procedure into a known repair. Unfamiliar or ambiguous cases still need escalation.

options.text: It supports tracing and undoing the repair where possible.
options.feedback: Recording the change and relevant prior information makes the intervention easier to inspect and reverse. It also preserves useful project state beyond the conversation.
